column1: # Game profile of The Patrick Star Game (Switch, update 1.0.1 = v1). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 2022.3 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 16.2.4; subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie (H.264 / AAC intro cinematics).

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory). Unity's nninitStartup (main+0x111fc00) queries TotalMemorySize − UsedMemorySize and passes it to
# nn::mem::StandardAllocator::Initialize as virtual address memory; with the 3.2 GB hardware pool (0xcd500000) that takes 3.14 GB of the 4.375 GB alias region, leaving too little
# address space for Unity's own AllocateAddressRegion calls (main+0x10fe9a0 SIGSEGV on NULL at frame 15). stdalloc_cap caps StandardAllocator's region at 960 MB (0x3c000000),
# matching the 1 GB-pool Unity 2022.3 profiles while preserving the 3.2 GB application pool
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 in the check boot: the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
